text: Fairmont's new AKS cluster is standing, but empty. This video brings grain-ingest — the service that receives scale-house weight readings during harvest — onto it for real: a production Dockerfile, a Helm chart wrapping the Deployment, Service, and a HorizontalPodAutoscaler, and the first live rollout.
Every pod this Deployment creates carries one label — app: grain-ingest — set in both the selector and the pod template, the same unremarkable choice any engineer would make.
That label is defined here, once, and every later lesson that needs to target these pods will read it rather than redefine it.
The HPA scales from three pods up to twenty as harvest traffic climbs, and back down once it passes — tested with a synthetic load spike before harvest ever puts real traffic on it.
grain-ingest is running, autoscaling correctly, and writing to Azure SQL. Next: a security pass that locks down exactly who's allowed to reach that database.
